=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package marks most clauses "[STANDARD]". It says they have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides". It also says the parties have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package". **I have reviewed every item anyway.** Those labels are the Seller's own assertion, not an agreed position. They also conflict with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. Para 11 says no "negotiation position or approval is included", and para 1.4 disclaims any admission.

**Action:** Please confirm with the Wattlebridge deal lead whether anything has in fact been agreed. Until then, reply that nothing is agreed until the full SPA is agreed, and that all positions remain open.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap of 30–50% of price (AUD 7.2m–12m), or 20% plus buy-side W&I insurance. The cap should apply **only** to general warranties, not to fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 40%, with a fallback of 25–30% if W&I is bound. **Reason:** The known exposures (Bluefen at 30% of revenue, the privacy incident, the IP gap) could plausibly exceed AUD 4.8m.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25k per claim. Basket of AUD 250k (~1% of price), with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated. Basket of ~0.5–1% on a **tipping** basis, so the whole amount is recoverable once the basket is exceeded. Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Accept a ~AUD 240k basket only if it tips. Counter the de minimis at AUD 10k with an aggregation language. **Reason:** A deductible basket permanently gives away the first AUD 250k of genuine loss.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Any limitation applies "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general warranties, so two audit cycles are covered. Tax claims should run 7 years, or until the ATO amendment period plus 60 days. Fundamental/title claims should run 7 years or the statutory limitation period. Specific indemnities should run until the matter is resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months, with express separate periods for each category. **Reason:** The "applies to all Claims" wording would quietly shorten tax and title claims to 18 months.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would sit under the general cap and time limit, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, capitalisation) capped at 100% of price. No de minimis or basket. Not subject to disclosure. 7-year or statutory time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has bought nothing, so a 20% cap is inappropriate.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud exception.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out removing all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance protection for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their officers or advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out. **Reason:** This is non-negotiable market practice. Silence invites argument over whether misleading conduct claims (ACL s 18 / Fair Trading Act 1987 (NSW)) are excluded.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Only specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter count. Each must be "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely impact", against identified warranties. There should be no general data room disclosure, or at most a narrow, indexed one. No disclosure should apply against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or the specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. **Reason:** As drafted, it would wipe out warranty protection for every DD issue, including the incident, the IP gap and the bonuses.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Ideally an express pro-sandbagging clause, where Buyer knowledge does not bar claims. As a fallback, the bar should apply only to matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and only to actual knowledge of named individuals. Constructive knowledge ("discoverable") should be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** The "discoverable" wording turns diligence into a waiver and penalises the Buyer for doing DD.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL 2 confirms that no final consent has been given and the cl 11.3 conditions have not been shown to be satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent that only the Buyer can waive. It is satisfied only by an unconditional written consent from Bluefen, in a form approved by the Buyer, together with evidence that all DD-002 cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived. The Seller should use best (or all reasonable) endeavours. The Buyer should be able to walk away or reprice if the condition is not met by the end date.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the current drafting and tighten. **Reason:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m, about 30% of revenue. A consent with unmet conditions attached is not a consent.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release of the ~AUD 3.2m facility "to be provided following Completion". DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** The facility treated as Debt and deducted from the price. It should be repaid from completion funds under a payoff letter, with signed releases of security and PPSR discharges delivered **at** Completion. Riverlark's change-of-control right (cl 8.1) should be waived pending repayment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** A post-Completion release leaves secured debt and an acceleration risk with the Buyer, which is inconsistent with the debt-free basis.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and do not appear in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses and all associated payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG and other on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses/Debt-like items. They should be deducted from the price and paid through payroll at Completion. A specific indemnity should cover any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** The Company, now owned by the Buyer, is the employer liable to pay. If the bonuses are left out of the funds flow, the Buyer effectively pays AUD 420k or more twice.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent requiring either (a) evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, with Ironquay's confirmation, plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials, or (b) the AUD 180k paid at Completion by deduction from the price. The indemnity should also be broadened to cover **all** loss from the Company not owning, or being unable to use, the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, re-development costs and business interruption. It should sit outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title does not pass until every fee is paid. The real risk is loss of the IP, not the AUD 180k invoice.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". DL 6 confirms that ~1,240 records went to an unintended external address and that access, scope and notification obligations are unresolved.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants: the investigation is completed, with Buyer oversight, and a Notifiable Data Breaches assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) is made, with notifications given if required.
  - A specific indemnity covering regulatory penalties and investigations (OAIC), third-party and customer claims, notification, remediation and forensic costs. It should sit outside the general cap and basket, not be subject to disclosure, and have a specific cap or escrow and a long tail.
  - A specific warranty that no other incidents exist.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** The Seller itself cannot say whether the incident is a notifiable breach, so it cannot also be "not material", and the disclosure would otherwise kill any warranty claim.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL 8 says they should be "read together" and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** A disclosure or specific warranty on whether each renewal is terminable, its term and the amounts committed. Any pre-Completion prepaid or accrued amounts should be treated as working capital or debt-like items in the price mechanics. The Buyer should approve any further renewals before Completion. Note the aggregation risk: if the three are treated as one "matter", the AUD 330k mostly falls within a AUD 250k deductible basket.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation without supporting evidence, and add the specific warranty plus price treatment. **Reason:** The related-renewal timing suggests a commitment entered into around the sale, and under the Seller's thresholds only about AUD 80k would be recoverable.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Separately defined General Warranty Claims, Fundamental Warranty Claims, Tax Claims, Specific Indemnity Claims and Fraud Claims. Each should have its own cap, thresholds, time limit and disclosure treatment, set out expressly. The default should be that a limitation applies **only** to the category it names.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and restructure clause 12. **Reason:** The default-to-all wording is the mechanism that collapses every other protection into the 20%/18-month general regime.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title rests on the DD-012 share register. DL 10 states the Buyer has not done its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** The Buyer's own verification against a current ASIC company extract and the original register, plus a check for options, convertibles, SAFEs, ESOP awards and encumbrances. At Completion, the Buyer should receive share certificates, signed transfers, PPSR releases over the shares, and confirmation that no rights over the shares exist. The fundamental title warranty should be capped at 100% of price, as in N-004.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on DD-012 alone. Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and make delivery a Completion deliverable. **Reason:** A register maintained by the Seller is the Seller's own record, and the Seller is trying to cap its title liability at 20%.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity covering all pre-Completion Company tax, including the bonus payroll tax and super. It should be dollar-for-dollar, outside the cap and basket, not subject to disclosure, last 7 years, and include conduct-of-claims rights.
  - IP warranties covering ownership and chain of title, including Ironquay, treated as fundamental or at least subject to an enhanced cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the claim that these are "settled". They remain open terms to be negotiated. **Reason:** Nothing in the package shows agreement, and the general regime is unsuitable for tax and core IP in an analytics business.

---

## Other items to note (not in the issue list)
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says these involve notification or assignment restrictions rather than share-sale consents. Counsel should confirm that reading by reviewing the full clauses. Make the lease notification a pre-Completion Seller covenant.
- **Suggested next step:** Send a covering response stating that all positions are open, then circulate the Buyer mark-up. I can draft the clause 12 limitation schedule and the specific indemnity clauses for N-009 to N-012 if helpful.
